research_mode: official Home Office primary statistics only; hate-crime definition, recording-system, survey-scope and comparability gates; no parcel, exact-location, candidate or business result claimed

sources.name: Hate-crime annual release scope
verified_claims: The annual bulletin covers hate crimes recorded by police in England and Wales for the year ending March 2025.
limitations: National release scope does not establish the risk or incident history of a parcel.

sources.name: Police and survey source distinction
verified_claims: The bulletin combines police-recorded hate-crime information with estimates from the Crime Survey for England and Wales.
limitations: Police and survey measures have different populations and must not be merged as equivalent records.

sources.name: Police trend reliability boundary
verified_claims: Improvements in crime recording and hate-crime identification mean police-recorded figures do not provide reliable hate-crime trends since 2014.
limitations: A recorded increase must not automatically be interpreted as an increase in underlying prevalence.

sources.name: Police-demand interpretation
verified_claims: Police-recorded hate crime provides a measure of hate-crime-related demand on police services.
limitations: Police demand is not a complete prevalence measure because not all hate crime is reported.

sources.name: Metropolitan Police system change
verified_claims: The Metropolitan Police Service changed to the CONNECT crime-recording system in February 2024.
limitations: Data before and after the system change are not automatically comparable.

sources.name: One-record-per-victim change
verified_claims: CONNECT creates a separate record for each victim, while the previous system could nest multiple offences under one incident report.
limitations: Record architecture changes can alter counts without a corresponding change in incidents.

sources.name: Legacy hate-flag overstatement
verified_claims: Under the legacy MPS system, a hate identifier attached to one nested offence could be applied to other offences in the same report.
limitations: Historic MPS hate-crime offence totals can be overstated and must not be treated as like-for-like trend data.

sources.name: MPS trend exclusion
verified_claims: MPS data for year ending March 2025 are excluded from trend analysis because they are not comparable with prior data.
limitations: England and Wales trend values excluding MPS must not be represented as all-force like-for-like totals.

sources.name: Perceived-hostility definition
verified_claims: Hate crime is defined by perception that a criminal offence was motivated by hostility or prejudice based on a personal characteristic.
limitations: A statistical flag does not independently prove motive to a criminal evidential standard.

sources.name: Five monitored strands
verified_claims: The five centrally monitored strands are race or ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, disability and transgender identity.
limitations: The five-strand collection is not a complete taxonomy of every hostility characteristic.

sources.name: Multiple motivating strands
verified_claims: A single offence can be flagged against more than one monitored hate-crime strand.
limitations: Summing strand counts can double-count offences and must not be used as the offence total.

sources.name: Flag-quality dependency
verified_claims: Hate-crime statistics depend on the relevant flag being correctly applied to the recorded offence.
limitations: An absent flag does not prove an offence lacked a hate motivation.

sources.name: Non-monitored characteristic boundary
verified_claims: Hostility based on characteristics such as age or gender is not included in the centrally monitored collection.
limitations: Exclusion from the collection does not mean such hostility or offences do not exist.

sources.name: Recording and prosecution distinction
verified_claims: A crime may be recorded as hate crime but prosecuted as such only where evidence of hostility is submitted in the case file.
limitations: A recorded hate flag must not be represented as a conviction or sentence uplift.

sources.name: Terrorism classification boundary
verified_claims: Terrorist offences may or may not be classified as hate crimes depending on whether a monitored strand was targeted.
limitations: Terrorism and hate-crime totals are not interchangeable datasets.

sources.name: Non-crime hate incident exclusion
verified_claims: The Home Office does not collect police data on non-crime hate incidents in this bulletin.
limitations: The bulletin cannot be used to estimate the volume of non-crime hate incidents.

sources.name: Three-year CSEW pooling
verified_claims: Three annual CSEW datasets are combined because single-year hate-crime estimates are too unreliable to report.
limitations: The pooled estimate is not a single-year point estimate.

sources.name: Short-term trend limitation
verified_claims: Combined three-year CSEW hate-crime estimates are unsuitable for examining short-term changes.
limitations: Month-to-month or annual local movement must not be inferred from the pooled survey estimate.

sources.name: CSEW recording independence
verified_claims: CSEW estimates include crimes not reported to police and are unaffected by police recording practices, reporting rates or police activity.
limitations: Survey estimates still carry sampling and coverage limitations.

sources.name: CSEW population and offence exclusions
verified_claims: The CSEW excludes businesses, people not resident in households, homicide and victimless offences such as many public-order crimes.
limitations: CSEW hate-crime estimates do not represent all populations or offence types.
